MASS (3), CONCENTRATION (4), PRUNE (4) and SNAP (9) rows already exist in ledger/submissions.csv; SPACING is the brief's lowest priority and TRACKB is Phase 2 only. RELIEF is the only unbuilt Week 1-2 axis in the brief's default plan. Recorded in IRREGULARITIES.md.

parent.label: R1
parent.why_not_R0: Brief v2 section 4.4 requires >=3 px from the catalogue for every non-PRUNE axis. R0 (h33-h33-2-b2) carries 2,171 dots at 2<d_cat<=3 px, so a RELIEF edit of R0 would be unspendable HOLD like the earlier R0-based MASS/CONCENTRATION families. SLOT_PLAN.md Week 2 already scheduled RELIEF on R1. R1 is rebuilt from the pinned lineage and BOTH published SHA-256 values are asserted before editing; if either mismatches the build aborts (never approximate the parent).
parent.live_score_evidence: R1 has no RECEIPT. Its grandparent R0 live 0.2778 is CLAIM (no receipt in ledger/). All deltas below are MODEL vs R1, never a score.

relief_definition.field: training_features.tif Band 12 det_elev (detrended elevation), cleaned exactly as scripts/build_prune_variants.py cleans bands (footprint-masked, NaN to 0, |x|>1e20 replaced by footprint median)
relief_definition.terciles: Footprint quantiles q1=Q(1/3), q2=Q(2/3) of Band 12 over the 5,167,373 footprint pixels, recomputed deterministically at build time and recorded to full float precision in evidence/relief_axis_report.json (diagnostic values 2026-10-23: q1 approx -143 m, q2 approx +38.6 m). Classes: T1 basin (det_elev<=q1), T2 piedmont/range-front (q1<det_elev<=q2), T3 range (det_elev>q2). Outside footprint: no class.
relief_definition.why_not_band19_or_local_relief: Pre-build diagnostic (registry/relief_diagnostic.json, reproduced by the build script): Band 19 det_elev_slope low tercile holds 0.47% of R0 dots and 279 H19-5 refill candidates; 1.1 km local-relief low tercile holds 1.00% of R0 dots and 450 candidates. A 10-15% shift into a flat-basin slope tercile is arithmetically infeasible from the parent's own H19-5 support and would require a new detector (changing the field, not the RELIEF axis; every field-replacement lane scored 0.00-0.19 CLAIM per the brief). Band 12 terciles have 12,851 / 25,616 / 20,843 refill candidates on the R1 basis. SLOT_PLAN.md also specified Band 12 det_elev terciles.
relief_definition.sgmc_warning: The USGS SGMC off-catalogue control is 63.6% T3 / 72.2% top slope tercile (a bedrock geologic-map compilation, biased to exposed range faults). Its relief gradient points opposite to the catalogue marginal-return gradient. Per Brief sections 3 and 6 it is REPORT ONLY, never a gate and never used to select donors or receivers. The bas2rng12 arm exists precisely so a live receipt can arbitrate between the two source populations.

allocation_algorithm: Count fixed at 37,654. Dose n_shift = round(0.12*37654) = 4,518 dots (11.9987% of parent; Brief RELIEF range 10-15%, change gate 1-50%). Step 1: drop the 4,518 parent dots in the SOURCE tercile with the lowest exact marginal DTI loss under the parent's own label-free corroboration field w (scripts/build_prune_variants.select_exact_marginal_dti_drop, the same ranking that built R1). Step 2: add the 4,518 un-emitted H19-5 ridge pixels in the TARGET tercile with the highest exact marginal DTI gain under the same w (select_exact_marginal_dti_add), candidates restricted to footprint, d_cat>3.0 px, target tercile. No RNG. Source/target terciles are disjoint, so no dropped dot can be re-added, the untouched tercile keeps its exact parent count, and every variant differs from R1 ONLY in relief-tercile allocation.

variants_fixed_before_any_proxy.rationale: Primary. Catalogue marginal return per dot is ~1.9x higher in T1 than T3 (ratio 2.41 vs 1.24) because R1 starves basin/piedmont dots relative to catalogue fault density. Post-shift shares (T1 32.4 / T2 41.8 / T3 25.8) near-match the catalogue relief allocation with a deliberate slight basin overshoot for alluvial burial incompleteness in the catalogue itself.

Range-front rival. T2 has the highest absolute catalogue fault density (14.36/1k) and hosts the range-front/piedmont systems the Faulds step-over inventory describes, but R1 already allocates T2 near its catalogue share, so the marginal-equalisation model predicts only a weak gain. Separates 'basin receivers were wasted' from 'range donors were valuable' if rng2bas12 fails.

Reverse bracket / falsification arm. This is the direction the bedrock-biased SGMC control prefers (SGMC truth-to-dot density ratio highest in T3). Under the primary (catalogue marginal + burial incompleteness) model it should lose: it starves T1 to ~8.4% of dots. Built as a diagnostic; spent live only if rng2bas12 returns <= R1-0.01, which would indicate the new-fault truth is SGMC-like bedrock faulting rather than catalogue-like relief allocation.

decision_rules.live_noise_floor: |delta| < 0.01 on the public chunks is no evidence (Brief section 5).
decision_rules.if_rng2bas12_ge_R1_plus_001: Basinward relief reallocation confirmed. Promote it as the new parent for a dose arm (rng2bas at +6% more or a catalogue-exact proportional allocation) and for combining with any other confirmed axis in Weeks 3-4.
decision_rules.if_rng2bas12_le_R1_minus_001: Primary relief hypothesis falsified in this direction. Spend the next relief slot on rng2pmt12 (tests whether T2 receivers save the axis) before ever considering bas2rng12; if rng2pmt12 also loses, range dots were load-bearing and RELIEF closes toward T3.
decision_rules.if_abs_delta_lt_001: No evidence from one public-chunk receipt. Do not build dose variants; carry rng2pmt12 as the bracket and prioritise the R1 collar receipt and a second orthogonal axis.

gates: Brief section 6 MUST gates only: format vs sample_submission.tif, zero catalogue mass, min d_cat>3 px asserted, SHA-256 not in ledger, parent-diff recorded, re-read from disk. Hide-and-recover PROXY (degenerate 0.0 for any >3 px file, IR-88-20), SGMC control and leakage canaries are REPORT ONLY.
